classification.difficultyReason: Translate named correlations into point patterns on supplied axes, controlling downward trend and scatter to distinguish weak, moderate and perfect relationships.

content.prompt: Draw a scatterplot with these correlations.

spec.description: Blank first-quadrant drawing axes with arrowheads and italic x and y labels; no ticks, numbers, grid or supplied points.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled Cartesian axes for a student-drawn strong positive correlation.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes always visible; points appear only in the solution.

answer.short: Example shown; points lie close to an upward-sloping straight line. Other suitable plots are acceptable.
answer.worked: As $x$ increases, $y$ tends to increase. Keep the points close to a straight line, with a little scatter.

spec.description: Authored acceptable example: black points close to an increasing straight line, with slight scatter.
Blank first-quadrant drawing axes with arrowheads and italic x and y labels; no ticks, numbers, grid or supplied points.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled Cartesian axes for a student-drawn weak negative correlation.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes always visible; points appear only in the solution.

answer.short: Example shown; widely scattered points have a slight downward trend. Other suitable plots are acceptable.
answer.worked: As $x$ increases, $y$ tends to decrease slightly. Use substantial scatter around this downward trend.

spec.description: Authored acceptable example: widely scattered black points with a slight decreasing linear trend.
Blank first-quadrant drawing axes with arrowheads and italic x and y labels; no ticks, numbers, grid or supplied points.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled Cartesian axes for a student-drawn perfect negative correlation.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes always visible; points appear only in the solution.

answer.short: Example shown; every point lies on one downward-sloping straight line. Other suitable plots are acceptable.
answer.worked: Place all points exactly on a straight line with negative gradient, so $y$ decreases as $x$ increases.

spec.description: Authored acceptable example: nine black points exactly collinear on a decreasing line.
Blank first-quadrant drawing axes with arrowheads and italic x and y labels; no ticks, numbers, grid or supplied points.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled Cartesian axes for a student-drawn scatterplot with no correlation.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes always visible; points appear only in the solution.

answer.short: Example shown; scattered points have no upward or downward trend. Other suitable plots are acceptable.
answer.worked: Scatter points without a clear linear trend. Increasing $x$ should not consistently increase or decrease $y$.

spec.description: Authored acceptable example: irregularly scattered black points without a clear rising or falling trend.
Blank first-quadrant drawing axes with arrowheads and italic x and y labels; no ticks, numbers, grid or supplied points.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled Cartesian axes for a student-drawn perfect positive correlation.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes always visible; points appear only in the solution.

answer.short: Example shown; every point lies on one upward-sloping straight line. Other suitable plots are acceptable.
answer.worked: Place all points exactly on a straight line with positive gradient, so $y$ increases as $x$ increases.

spec.description: Authored acceptable example: nine black points exactly collinear on an increasing line.
Blank first-quadrant drawing axes with arrowheads and italic x and y labels; no ticks, numbers, grid or supplied points.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled Cartesian axes for a student-drawn moderate negative correlation.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes always visible; points appear only in the solution.

answer.short: Example shown; points have a downward linear trend with moderate scatter. Other suitable plots are acceptable.
answer.worked: As $x$ increases, $y$ tends to decrease. Use more scatter than for a strong correlation, but keep the downward trend clearer than for a weak correlation.

spec.description: Authored acceptable example: black points with a decreasing linear trend and moderate scatter.
